After a long silence, Marge turns to Norm and says she is going to sleep. Norm murmurs a response, his eyes still fixed on the screen. Marge rolls over. Outside, snow begins to fall, drifting silently past the darkened windows of their house. The street is still. The traffic light blinks red. The snow continues to fall.

name: Marge Receives a Late-Night Call from Mike Yanagita
description: Marge is in bed with Norm, watching a nature program about insects on the television. After the show ends, Norm keeps staring at the screen while Marge says she’s going to sleep. She rolls over, and the room falls quiet except for Norm’s snoring. The phone rings. Marge reaches for it in the dark. A man’s voice asks if she’s Marge, then clarifies it’s Mike Yanagita. She recognizes the name and sits up. Mike says he saw her on the news covering the shootings in Brainerd and wasn’t sure it was really her. They exchange greetings. Marge asks what time it is. Mike says it’s nearly eleven and hopes he didn’t wake her. She says it’s fine. He mentions he’s down in the Twin Cities. They talk briefly about how long it’s been. Mike expresses surprise at seeing her on TV. Marge confirms it was her. They say it’s good to hear from each other.

The customer says he doesn’t need the sealant, and Jerry quickly agrees, dropping the offer. Jerry then shifts to financing, suggesting the customer consider the GMAC plan, calling it a great deal. description: Jerry is at work on the sales floor when another salesman interrupts to tell him he has a phone call. He steps away and answers the phone. On the other end, Carl speaks sharply, telling Jerry that there’s been bloodshed in Brainerd and that the ransom is now the full eighty thousand dollars. Jerry stammers in shock, protesting the change, but Carl cuts him off with a threat before hanging up abruptly. Jerry slams the receiver down just as the phone rings again. It’s a GMAC representative, asking about missing vehicle identification numbers. Jerry hesitates, then says they’re already in the mail. As soon as he hangs up, he knocks the blotter off his desk in a burst of frustration, sending pens scattering across the floor. He sits still for a moment, then slowly picks up the pens and straightens the blotter, placing everything back in order.
